s.note: Thin golden fries, salted straight out of the oil.
s.how: Cut 1kg russets into thin chips and soak in cold water for 30 minutes, then dry well. Fry at 140C for 5 minutes, rest, then fry at 190C until golden and crisp. Salt straight away and serve hot.

s.note: Thick-cut onion rings in crisp beer batter, stacked high with house sauce, argued over at the barbershop next door.
s.how: Thick onion rings dusted in flour, dipped in a cold lager batter and fried at 180C until crisp, stacked high with house sauce. Slice 3 large brown onions 1.5cm thick and separate the rings. Toss in 50g plain flour. Whisk 150g plain flour, 1 tsp baking powder and 1 tsp salt with 250ml cold lager until smooth. Dip the rings and fry in batches for 3 minutes until golden, then drain and salt. Stir 125g mayonnaise with 2 tbsp sweet pickle relish, 1 tsp American mustard, 1/2 tsp paprika and 1 tsp white vinegar for the house sauce.

m.note: Double smashed patties with special sauce on a three-piece bun.
m.how: Mix 100g mayo, 2 tbsp relish, 1 tsp mustard, paprika and a dash of vinegar. Smash 8 thin patties from 800g mince, add cheese. Build each in a plain seedless three-piece bun with sauce, shredded iceberg, diced onion and pickles.

w.note: Crisp baked pastry pocket of hot cinnamon apple and brown sugar, McDowell's own version.
w.how: Shortcrust pockets filled with hot cinnamon apple and brown sugar, crimped and baked at 200C until crisp. Cook 3 diced Granny Smith apples with 30g butter, 40g brown sugar, 1 tsp cinnamon and 1 tbsp lemon juice for 8 minutes, then thicken with 1 tsp cornflour in a splash of water and cool. Cut 2 sheets shortcrust pastry into 4 rectangles each, fill one half, fold, crimp with a fork and cut two slits. Brush with beaten egg, sprinkle with raw sugar and bake at 200C for 22 minutes.

d.note: Thick vanilla shakes blended with plenty of ice cream.
d.how: For each shake, blend 3 scoops vanilla ice cream with 150ml cold milk until thick and smooth. Pour into a chilled tall glass and serve with a wide straw. Make four, one after the other, so they stay thick.
